Simulate a fishery conditional on population mortality

Source: R/sim_fishery.R
sim_fishery.Rd

Allocate existing mortality using a share, fully selected F, or catch target, generate aggregate catches, and simulate catch reporting and nested biological monitoring. Omitting sim creates a configuration without running a simulation or drawing random values.

sim_fishery(
  sim,
  target,
  catch_model,
  selectivity = sim_logistic(),
  selectivity_by = "age",
  gear_amount = 1,
  duration = 1,
  gear_unit = "gear_unit",
  time_unit = "time_unit",
  targeting = 1,
  knowledge_sd = 0,
  exploration = 0.05,
  subset_cells,
  n_sims = NULL,
  max_operations = 10000,
  reporting_factor = 1,
  reporting_cv = 0,
  sampling_coverage = 1,
  sampling_targeting = 0,
  lengths_cap = 100,
  ages_cap = 5,
  age_sampling = "stratified",
  age_length_group = 1,
  light = TRUE,
  maturity_sampling = "aged",
  target_type = "share"
)

Arguments

sim

A simulation list from sim_distribution(). May be omitted to create a sim_fishery_spec configuration.

target

A nonnegative scalar or vector aligned with simulation years. Its meaning is set by target_type.

catch_model

Function (available, operation) returning one whole-fish proposal per available row, between zero and its remaining N. See sim_capture() for the table contract and a generic built-in model.

selectivity

Function returning probabilities in [0, 1], evaluated on ages or growth-model length-group labels. Values are not rescaled.

selectivity_by

Either "age" or "length".

gear_amount, duration

Positive settings, or functions of an operation record returning one positive number. Their product is nominal effort.

gear_unit, time_unit

Nonempty labels for gear and time units.

targeting

Nonnegative exponent controlling preference for high estimated vulnerable density. Zero gives uniform locations.

knowledge_sd

Nonnegative map-error SD, expressed as a multiple of initial mean accessible vulnerable density. Errors are redrawn for each replicate/year and persist across its operations. Location choice uses that year's current vulnerable density plus these errors, updating density after catches. This is noisy contemporaneous knowledge, without learning or a lagged distribution map.

exploration

Proportion of location probabilities allocated uniformly, in [0, 1]. All-zero estimated densities fall back to uniform locations.

subset_cells

Logical expression evaluated on grid columns and year, restricting accessible cells. By default all cells are accessible.

n_sims

Replicate count. NULL inherits batch metadata, otherwise one. An explicit count must agree with existing batch metadata.

max_operations

Maximum operations per fishery, replicate and year.

reporting_factor, reporting_cv

Mean and CV of operation-level lognormal reporting multipliers. The same multiplier applies to numbers and kilograms.

sampling_coverage

Expected proportion of operations selected for biological sampling, in [0, 1].

sampling_targeting

Nonnegative preference for high reported catches. Inclusion probabilities are calibrated to the requested expected coverage.

lengths_cap

Maximum fish measured per selected operation.

ages_cap

Maximum measured fish aged per operation ("random") or per operation and length group ("stratified").

age_sampling

Either "stratified" or "random".

age_length_group

Positive length-bin width for stratified age sampling.

light

If FALSE, retain joint age-length catches and sample truth.

maturity_sampling

Fish examined for maturity: "aged" (default), "measured", or "none". Binary states follow the population maturity model. Unexamined mature values are missing and maturity_observed is FALSE. With light = FALSE, sample_truth retains latent states for measured fish. All length/age sampling finishes before maturity is drawn for every measured fish, independently of this observation mask. Switching only this argument preserves existing samples, catches, and overlapping maturity states. An older object lacking a maturity model can retain number-only sampling with "none". For each measured fish, samp$age_probability and samp$maturity_probability record its inclusion probabilities conditional on measurement. Both are missing for unmeasured fish.

target_type

One of "share" (default: proportion of Z before selectivity, in [0, 1]), "F_full" (annual fishing mortality at selectivity one), "catch_n" (fish), or "catch_kg" (kilograms).

Value

The simulation list with replicates and a fishery list containing setdet (operation details), catch_at_age, catch_at_length, sp_removals, mortality_ledger, samp, annual, reference, settings, and named configurations. Identifiers link fishery, replicate (sim), year, operation, and sample. True counts are integers; reported numbers can be fractional. annual records target_type, requested_target (the supplied setting), reference_target and target (continuous and operational stopping targets), target_unit, achieved, and shortfall. It also retains expected reference catches as reference_target_n and reference_target_kg, and F_full_reference (missing for share targets, whose F also depends on Z at age). reference includes kg_reference at age. Reference biomass uses the growth key; a particular integer length-stock realization can have different biomass. CPUE is catch divided by nominal effort; annual CPUE uses totals. Biomass and biomass CPUE use the weight relationship stored by sim_abundance(). With light = FALSE, joint_catch and sample_truth are also retained. Without sim, a sim_fishery_spec list.

Details

Numeric controls may be scalar or year-aligned vectors; named vectors must name every year. Gear callbacks receive identifiers, location, and resolved gear settings. They must not implement hidden seeding. The capture table uses age, length, N, selectivity, and cell_area; operations include fishery, sim, year, operation, cell, gear_amount, duration, and effort. Grid area and capture-model units must agree.

For length-age probabilities P and selectivity s, mean selectivity at age is s_bar = sum(P * s). Share targets set F_reference = target * Z * s_bar; fully selected F targets set F_reference = target * s_bar, without rescaling selectivity. Catch targets scale that same selectivity pattern to the requested expected numbers or kilograms using the Baranov equation under fixed Z. Kilograms integrate weight jointly with length selectivity, not as a product of separately averaged weight and selectivity.

Targets must be finite and nonnegative. Catch targets cannot exceed starting N or B, and must fit the mortality available under Z and selectivity. Reference F, including combined fisheries, cannot exceed Z at any age/year. Combined reference catches must also fit starting N and B, including when length selectivity concentrates several fisheries on the same heavy fish. Errors identify the fishery/year and applicable limits before stock allocation draws. Valid targets can still have shortfalls due to access, capture response, operation limits, integer rounding or shared-stock constraints.

Shares, F_full and catch_n stop at the rounded reference total in numbers. These reference catches are rounded jointly across fisheries, with the rounded combined total capped at the shared integer death count. Catch_kg stops at the requested kilograms using realized catch weights, not a converted number quota. Whole fish are retained; final catches are thinned proportionally in aggregate, then filled with randomly selected categories of fish that fit. No individual commercial catch records are generated. A residual kilogram shortfall can remain when no eligible whole fish fits; status is exhausted. Zero-weight fish do not provide a positive kilogram catching opportunity. Realized age composition may differ from the reference, so meeting a catch target need not reproduce reference F or one exact realized F_full. Age-specific death budgets preserve the rounded total expected deaths using largest-remainder rounding. Fishing and residual other deaths share those budgets. Residual deaths are sampled from remaining fish without replacement. reference retains N, Z, shared integer total_deaths, reference and realized catches, U_realized = catch_realized / N, and F_realized at age. total_deaths is the whole-fish total implied by N and Z for that age/year, balanced-rounded across ages. It includes all fishery and other deaths, and is repeated in each fishery's reference rows; do not sum it across fisheries. It is neither an individual catch target nor a remaining allowance. At the end it equals the ledger's fishery plus other deaths. death_budget remains an identical compatibility alias; new code should prefer total_deaths. Realized F is the Baranov-equivalent U_realized * Z / (1 - exp(-Z)) under fixed upstream Z, not a fitted operation-time hazard. With positive N and zero Z it is zero; with zero N both realized rates are missing. Integer rounding can make combined equivalent F exceed Z in tiny populations; values are not clipped. Matching the total number target need not match F at every age.

Effort determines allocation and required operations conditional on the catch budget; it cannot independently increase annual removals. The final operation retains all specified effort when capped by the target (quota_limited). Zero-catch operations retain their effort. Unreachable targets return a shortfall and termination status. A shortfall is the stopping target minus true catch, in target_unit (fish or kg): exhausted means no eligible accessible catching opportunities remain (including known zero capture/capacity); operation_limit means the allowed operations ended before reaching the target. Unused fishing allocation becomes other deaths under the fixed total-mortality budget. Local removals do not feed back into later pre-generated populations, and are not subtracted again from future abundance. Other mortality can include other fisheries. All simulated catches are retained; discards and seasonal scheduling are outside this model. Unnamed mortality matrices from custom closures use the age/year order of sim_abundance(); supplied dimension labels must agree with the population.

Fishing truth is completed before monitoring. Biological samples are drawn from actual catches, with ages nested within measured fish. Sample records contain stage-specific inclusion probabilities, missing unobserved ages, and weight in kilograms per measured fish from the population's weight-at-length relationship. The maturity_probability is conditional on a fish being measured and is one, the conditional aging probability, or zero for the measured, aged, or none maturity protocols, respectively. Catch, stock and mortality tables remain aggregate even for very large stocks.

See also

vignette("fisheries", package = "SimSurvey") for controlled comparisons of targeting, knowledge, reporting, and biological monitoring. run_catch() summarizes reported catch and estimates its length and age composition from monitoring records.

Examples

capture <- sim_capture(q = 0.1, capacity_per_gear = 50)
specification <- sim_fishery(target = 0.2, catch_model = capture)
f_target <- sim_fishery(target = 0.1, target_type = "F_full", catch_model = capture)
number_target <- sim_fishery(target = 100, target_type = "catch_n", catch_model = capture)
mass_target <- sim_fishery(target = 50, target_type = "catch_kg", catch_model = capture)
# \donttest{
population <- sim_abundance(ages = 1:3, years = 1:2) |>
  sim_distribution(grid = make_grid(res = c(20, 20)))
result <- sim_fishery(population, target = 0.2, catch_model = capture,
                      max_operations = 100)
result$fishery$annual
